text:
Lee (eng-runtime): @channel SSE streams showing large tail latency and periodic stalls, started ~10:12 UTC. p95 ~380ms -> 1.4s, p99 spikes to 8-12s on a subset of requests. Seeing chunking gaps in proxy logs. :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): paging oncall. I'm on it. Any customer reports yet?
Sara (customer-success): CS flagged 2 customers reporting timeouts in dashboards. They see rebuffering in the UI and messages 'response stalled'.
Jordan (eng-sre): throwing up graphs now — looks like sudden increase in server-side chunk gaps (bytes not flushed) around 10:11:30. Proxy (edge-nginx) shows repeated 504s with 'upstream timed out' for streaming paths.
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-2145. Severity: P1. Paging 'oncall' group.
Lee (eng-runtime): hypothesis: client backpressure + proxy buffering + small write batching => kernel-level bursts and occasional stall when buffer fills. Also saw increase in upstream CPU steal on a box in region-us-east-1b.
Ash (eng-platform): I can scale the streaming fleet and adjust proxy config temporarily. Suggest increasing proxy_read_timeout and enabling chunked_transfer_encoding bypass for streaming endpoints.
Maya (oncall): Assigning roles: Lee = triage lead, Jordan = logs/metrics, Ash = mitigation ops, Sara = customer comms.
Lee (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally with a test client that simulates slow consumer. The runtime currently writes 8KB frames every 200ms; if the client window shrinks we accumulate 1-2MB before kernel backpressure triggers and the runtime stalls waiting on write.
Jordan (eng-sre): Relevant logs excerpt:
```
[10:11:32] proxy: upstream write timeout, bytes_sent=10240, upstream_addr=10.4.3.12
[10:11:33] runtime: stalled sending chunk, pending_kv=1.2MB, conn_fd=42
[10:11:34] kernel: EAGAIN on write_n, backlog=2048
```
Lee (eng-runtime): Also p95/p99 by model: small-models unaffected, large-model streaming (>=2k tokens) show worst tail. That tracks with longer-lived KV cache and bigger chunk sizes.
Sara (customer-success): Which customers are impacted?
Maya (oncall): Sara, sending list via DM. Affected customers currently: acme-inc, skycart, trial-org-45 (low volume).
Sara (customer-success): OK will open interim tickets and offer a mitigation note.
Ash (eng-platform): Rolling temporary proxy change to bypass buffering for /v1/stream endpoints. Patch: nginx snippet to forward chunked flushes immediately:
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
proxy_read_timeout 120s;
```
DeployBot: Starting canary deploy of proxy config to region-us-east-1b (2/6 hosts).
Jordan (eng-sre): Adding filter to drop connections that exceed 60s idle during an active stream (so we can break dead slow clients rather than stall everyone).
Lee (eng-runtime): Also enabling internal 'flush-on-token' mode for the streaming runtime: flush after every token rather than batch every 200ms. This increases p50 slightly but removes the large tail. Triggering on a runtime flag: STREAM_FLUSH_STRATEGY=token.
Maya (oncall): Please coordinate canary windows and rollbacks. If any errors spike, revert immediately.
Lee (eng-runtime): Canary started. Initial canary hosts show p95 down to ~220ms, p99 down to ~900ms. No increase in error rate so far.
Jordan (eng-sre): Observed one proxy 502 during canary failover — small spike but within thresholds. Monitoring.
Sara (customer-success): Notifying impacted customers: sending email template with mitigation steps and ETA 30m.
Ash (eng-platform): Canary successful on 2 hosts. Rolling to rest of us-east. Rolling config includes explicit small write size limit and disabling proxy buffering.
DeployBot: Rolling config to remaining 4 hosts in region-us-east-1b. Progress: 4/4 done.
Maya (oncall): Patch rolled. How are the metrics?
Jordan (eng-sre): After full roll: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms for streaming. Tail stalls eliminated in region. Global aggregate improved but still small residuals from other regions — investigating.
Lee (eng-runtime): Follow-up: we need longer-term fix — options: adaptive flush strategy (based on client RTT/backpressure), chunk-size tuning per model length, kernel-level write timeout handling to avoid blocking scheduler, and improved observability to attribute stalls to slow consumers vs proxy.
Ash (eng-platform): Filed ENG-PLAT-783: add adaptive flusher + per-route proxy config. Also PR to add healthcheck that reports 'streaming_tailroom' metric from runtime.
Jordan (eng-sre): Postmortem checklist: capture flamegraphs for write syscalls, collect runtime traces around stalled connections, add alert for sustained p99>1s on streaming routes.
Sara (customer-success): Customers notified, some accepted status update. We'll follow up with a slimmed-down post-incident note and rollback URL.
Maya (oncall): Handing off to Lee for post-incident engineering. I'm leaving oncall in 22 minutes — tagging @next-oncall.
Lee (eng-runtime): Thanks — I'll draft a short incident summary and action items. Preliminary customer impact: ~0.2% requests experienced rebuffering, 3 customers reported UX issues. No data loss.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-2145 marked "mitigated" at 10:21:18 UTC.
Lee (eng-runtime): Postmortem owner: Lee. ETA for draft: EOD. Action items: (1) adaptive flush strategy (owner: Lee), (2) proxy default change to disable buffering for streaming routes (owner: Ash), (3) alert rule for streaming p99 (owner: Jordan), (4) customer follow-up (owner: Sara).
Sara (customer-success): Adding notes to customer tickets and scheduling follow-up calls where needed.
Jordan (eng-sre): Leaving a query for monitoring team to surface root cause: correlate kernel write blocking with container CPU steal and network egress bursts.
Ash (eng-platform): I'll open infra follow-up to ensure autoscaling triggers earlier for streaming nodes.
Lee (eng-runtime): Thanks all. Closing thread but will post the postmortem link here when ready.
Maya (oncall): Oncall signoff: leaving to next-oncall with the handoff doc in #oncall-handoffs. :thumbsup:
